memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Determine the distances involved and divide into three parts the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that a person who kills someone may flee for refuge. This is the rule concerning anyone who kills a person and flees there for safety—anyone who kills a neighbor unintentionally, without malice aforethought. - Deut 19:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gave careful, practical instructions. The land was to be divided into three parts, with roads prepared, so that the cities of refuge would be reachable. Someone who had accidentally killed a neighbour, without hatred or intent, needed to be able to reach safety quickly. God did not want mercy to be technically available yet practically out of reach.

This is a beautiful glimpse into God's character. He does not make His mercy hard to find. He carefully arranged for the roads to be clear and the cities to be within reach, so that the one who needed refuge could actually get there in time. Mercy was not hidden away; it was made accessible.

How this reflects the gospel. God has not made His salvation distant or difficult to reach. In Christ, He has come near to us, opening the way and clearing the road so that anyone who flees to Him can find refuge. The New Testament tells us that the word of salvation is near, in our mouths and in our hearts (Rom 10:8-9). We do not have to climb to heaven or cross the sea to find God's mercy; He has brought it near in Jesus. What a kind God, who not only provides refuge but makes sure we can reach it. Have you run to the refuge that God has placed so near to you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you realise how near God's mercy is in Christ?
2. What keeps you from running to Him for refuge?
3. How can you help others find the road to His mercy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for bringing Your mercy near in Jesus. Help me run to You without delay, and help others find the way too. Amen.
